title: Pull-request session-author identities
description: The list scripts/pr_session_identity.py reads to decide whether a pull request's AUTHOR is one of the maintainer's session accounts, and so whether the session conventions (the [via] title, the issue-link trailer and the promote marker) apply to it (req-dev-multisession-session-author-scope). An entry is an identity, not a name: the numeric GitHub account id and the type User authorize together; the login is diagnostics. The file is read by a stdlib-only host tool (shape-checked at load, fail-closed) and validated against this schema by tap/tests/test_pr_session_identity.py.

description.description: Why this file exists, what it governs, and what is deliberately absent from it.

authors.description: The maintainer's session accounts. Order is irrelevant; ids are unique. An empty list would silently exempt the maintainer's own sessions, so at least one entry is required.

login.description: The account login as GitHub reports it, for diagnostics and audit. Never used for authorization.

id.description: GitHub's numeric account id (github.event.pull_request.user.id), the authorizing identity, read from GitHub's /users/<login> response, never guessed.

type.description: GitHub account type as /users/<login> reports it. Session accounts are human accounts, so only User is valid; the authenticated author's type must equal it.

verified.description: The date the id/type/login triple was read from GitHub.

note.description: Whose account this is and why its pull requests carry the session conventions.
